title: Ordinary module tensor equations for coefficient change
statement:
Let R,S be sheaves of commutative rings on two small sites, f a ringed pullback and k its normalized module tensor comparison [def-pur-cochain-tensor-coherence-data]. Let d be a compatible coefficient square R to Rprime and S to Sprime, fprime=changed(f,d), and kprime a normalized comparison for fprime [def-pur-cochain-coefficient-arrows]. Write F=f.L, Fprime=fprime.L, E_R=extensionFunctor(d.sourceMap), E_S=extensionFunctor(d.targetMap), and U=restrictionFunctor(d.targetMap). Let b:E_R composed with Fprime to F composed with E_S be scalarAssociation(f,k,d,kprime), and t=transitionModule(f,k,d,kprime):F to E_R composed with Fprime composed with U. Denote the extension tensor comparisons by e_R,e_S, and restrictionTensorModule(d.targetMap,A,B):UA tensor_S UB to U(A tensor_Sprime B) by r(A,B). Then for all R-module sheaves M,N the following equations hold, with a semicolon denoting composition in order of application:
$$F'(e_R(M,N));k'(E_RM,E_RN);(b_M\otimes b_N)=b_{M\otimes_RN};E_S(k(M,N));e_S(FM,FN),$$
$$k(M,N);(t_M\otimes t_N);r(F'E_RM,F'E_RN)=t_{M\otimes_RN};U\bigl(F'(e_R(M,N));k'(E_RM,E_RN)\bigr).$$
The first equation is Sprime-linear; the second is S-linear with the displayed restriction of scalars. Coefficient maps need not be invertible; quotient maps and zero rings are allowed. These are ordinary module equations with no total complexes or differentials.

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-module-tensor-extension-equation for the extension square. For the transition square use naturality of the extension comparison and the extension/restriction adjunction. For arbitrary maps a:X to U(P), b:Y to U(Q), expansion of homEquiv and unit naturality identify (a tensor b) followed by the restriction tensor mate with the adjunction unit followed by U(mu; (L(a);counit tensor L(b);counit)). Apply this to the unit followed by restricted inverse scalar association. The adjunction triangles replace each adjunct by the inverse association. Unit naturality moves the original tensor comparison inside U, and cancellation with the three association isomorphisms reduces the result exactly to the extension square. This is a formal categorical proof, with no generator-generation assumption or invertibility of coefficient maps.

from.place: Canonical tensor comparison used for coefficient twists: parent cochain coherence proof step 6.

lean.statement:
theorem cochainModuleTensorCoefficients (f : RingedPullback R S) (k : Comparison f)
    (d : CoefficientSquare f) (k' : Comparison (changed f d)) :
    (∀ M N : Modules R,
      (changed f d).L.map ((extensionComparison d.sourceMap).mu M N).hom ≫
          (k'.mu ((extensionFunctor d.sourceMap).obj M)
            ((extensionFunctor d.sourceMap).obj N)).hom ≫
          ((scalarAssociation f k d k').hom.app M ⊗ₘ
            (scalarAssociation f k d k').hom.app N) =
        (scalarAssociation f k d k').hom.app (M ⊗ N) ≫
          (extensionFunctor d.targetMap).map (k.mu M N).hom ≫
          ((extensionComparison d.targetMap).mu (f.L.obj M) (f.L.obj N)).hom) ∧
    (∀ M N : Modules R,
      (k.mu M N).hom ≫
          ((transitionModule f k d k').app M ⊗ₘ (transitionModule f k d k').app N) ≫
          restrictionTensorModule d.targetMap
            ((changed f d).L.obj ((extensionFunctor d.sourceMap).obj M))
            ((changed f d).L.obj ((extensionFunctor d.sourceMap).obj N)) =
        (transitionModule f k d k').app (M ⊗ N) ≫ (restrictionFunctor d.targetMap).map
          ((changed f d).L.map ((extensionComparison d.sourceMap).mu M N).hom ≫
            (k'.mu ((extensionFunctor d.sourceMap).obj M)
              ((extensionFunctor d.sourceMap).obj N)).hom))
